seed: tools/stream_seed.js · total 45 · crash at event 4
CHARGE A CARD EXACTLY ONCE — FOUR STAGES
three guards, and the one place the truth actually lives
replayable source (offset)
re-readable from a committed offset — protects COMPLETENESS
dedup shuffle
a seen-set of record ids — protects accuracy for 1 of 3 crash windows
idempotent sink (idempotency key)
key "order-4", derived from the data — covers 3 of 3
external system
the only component that can know the charge happened
Only the last stage is outside the pipeline, and it holds the one fact that matters: whether order-4 has already been charged.
Every mechanism in the first three stages is about not having to know that — and only the idempotency key actually asks.
Step 1/4 — the pipeline, and the one stage that touches the world
Four stages, and the design's whole difficulty is that the decisive fact lives in the fourth. The source protects completeness and has no
substitute; the dedup shuffle covers 1 of 3 crash windows; the idempotency key covers 3. Note that the third mechanism depends on the external
system offering it — the design has a dependency it cannot satisfy itself.
System design — charge a card exactly once
order 4, amount 6: crash after the charge, replay, charged 6 not 12
seed: tools/stream_seed.js · total 45 · crash at event 4
THE CRASH-AND-RETRY SEQUENCE FOR ORDER 4 (amount 6)
five steps, one charge
1. record id 4 passes the dedup shuffle
seen-set gains id 4
2. sink calls charge("order-4", 6)
processor charges 6 and records the key
3. the pipeline crashes before committing the offset
the charge happened; the pipeline does not know it
4. replay re-reads from the old offset
record id 4 arrives again — and the seen-set was lost with the crash
5. sink calls charge("order-4", 6) again
processor recognises the key → no second charge
total charged
6, not 12
Step 4 is the one that defeats dedup: the seen-set was in memory and died with the process, so the replayed record looks new.
Only the key survives the crash, because it lives in the processor. That is why the key is the mechanism and the shuffle is an optimisation.
Step 2/4 — the retry, traced — order 4 charged once
Step 4 is where the earlier redundancy breaks down concretely: the dedup seen-set lived in the crashed process, so after the restart the replayed
record is indistinguishable from a new one. The only state that survived the crash is in the payment processor, and the only mechanism that reads
it is the idempotency key. Total charged 6, not 12.
System design — charge a card exactly once

seed: tools/stream_seed.js · total 45 · crash at event 4
IDEMPOTENT EFFECT VS DISTRIBUTED TRANSACTION
both reach exactly-once; one of them keeps working when something fails
idempotent effect (an idempotency key)
one round trip · the processor decides · retry is free
two-phase commit
prepare + commit · a coordinator must not fail between them
what 2PC buys
exactly-once even when the external system has no key
what it costs
a blocking coordinator, and an in-doubt state with no safe default
A coordinator that dies after "prepare" leaves the charge in doubt: committing may double-charge, aborting may lose a legitimate payment.
So prefer an idempotent effect whenever the external system allows one, and treat 2PC as what you do when it does not.
Step 3/4 — two-phase commit is the alternative, and it is worse
Two-phase commit genuinely achieves exactly-once across a side effect, and it is the right answer when the external system has no idempotency key.
The reason to prefer the key is in the note: 2PC has a state — prepared, coordinator gone — in which neither committing nor aborting is safe, and
that state has to be resolved by a human.
System design — charge a card exactly once
order 4, amount 6: crash after the charge, replay, charged 6 not 12
seed: tools/stream_seed.js · total 45 · crash at event 4
SCOPE
The idempotency key requires the processor to support it. If it does not, this design does not degrade gracefully — it is simply unavailable, and
2PC is the fallback.
The key must be derived from the data ("order-4"). A key generated at send time produces a second charge with extra steps, and nothing in the
pipeline detects that.
The dedup seen-set is unbounded state. Bounding it by a window means dedup stops working past that horizon — so the 1-of-3 coverage is also
time-limited.
And a replayable source protects completeness only as far back as its retention. Beyond that, the 23 outcome is reachable again and no downstream
guard helps.
Step 4/4 — and what this design does NOT settle
The first two gaps are the ones that silently break this design. The whole guarantee rests on a feature of someone else's system, and on a key
being derived from data rather than generated — and a send-time key fails in a way that produces a correct-looking pipeline and a double charge.
Neither is visible from inside, which is why both belong in the design review rather than in testing.
